recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-29315; do not reintroduce the older triggering-resource wording because later accepted issues superseded that terminology.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I issue asking to add Subscription.maxCount 0..1 positiveInteger with _count-like maximum semantics, allowing fewer results and excluding supporting bundle entries from the count limit.
initial_application: Commit dbeb5e6a7aa3cba0705a1c337c0eaf6174d32eb2 applied FHIR#29315 by adding maxCount to the Subscription spreadsheet source and an example. The later source rework commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 carried the element into source/subscription/structuredefinition-Subscription.xml as Subscription.maxCount 0..1 positiveInt.
additional_context: The Subscription resource is active in source/fhir.ini. The origin Zulip thread and FHIR-I minutes align with the Jira request. Later issues FHIR-39467 and FHIR-50622 refined the wording from triggering resources to events and added batching narrative, explaining why current source intentionally uses event-based wording.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current structuredefinition-Subscription.xml defines Subscription.maxCount as 0..1 positiveInt with the maximum-event and dependent-resource exception, and subscription-notes.xml explains servers SHALL NOT include more than the specified number of events in a notification bundle.
